{{short description|General form of integrable system}}
{{Distinguish|Kundu–Eckhaus equation}}
{{Technical|date=August 2020}}

The '''Kundu equation''' is a general form of [[integrable system]] that is gauge-equivalent to the mixed [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]]. It was proposed by Anjan Kundu<ref name={{kundu|1984}} >
{{citation | first=A. |last=Kundu |title=Landau–Lifshitz and higher-order nonlinear systems gauge generated from nonlinear Schrödinger-type equations | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | volume=25 |issue=12 | year=1984 |pages=3433–3438 |doi=10.1063/1.526113|bibcode = 1984JMP....25.3433K }}
</ref> as
{{NumBlk||<math display="block"> i q_t + q_{xx} + i\alpha (| q|^2q)_x + c |q|^2q
-(\theta_t+ \theta_x^2-i\theta_{xx} )q + \theta_x( 2iq_x
- \alpha | q|^2 q)=0, </math>|{{EquationRef|1}}}}
with arbitrary function <math> \theta (t,x) </math> and the subscripts denoting partial derivatives. Equation (1) is shown to be reducible for the choice of <math> \theta_{x} = -\kappa |q|^2 </math> to an integrable class of mixed [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]] with cubic–quintic nonlinearity, given in a representative form
{{NumBlk||<math display="block"> q_t + q_{xx} + i\alpha (| q|^2q)_x + c |q|^2q + \gamma |q|^4q + 4i \kappa (| q|^2)_x q = 0 . </math>|{{EquationRef|2}}}}
Here <math> \alpha, c, \kappa </math> are independent parameters, while <math> \gamma = \kappa(4 \kappa + \alpha) . </math> Equation {{EquationNote|1|(1)}}, more specifically equation {{EquationNote|2|(2)}} is known as the '''Kundu equation'''.<ref name={{FengW|2006}}/>

==Properties and applications==

The Kundu equation is a completely [[integrable system]], allowing [[Lax pair]] representation, exact solutions, and higher [[conserved quantity]].
Along with its different particular cases, this equation has been investigated for finding its exact [[travelling wave]] solutions,<ref name={{Zhang|2010}}>{{citation|first= H. |last= Zhang |title= Various exact travelling wave solutions for Kundu equation with fifth order nonlinear terms|journal= Rep. Math. Phys.|volume=65|issue= 2 |year=2010|page= 231|doi= 10.1016/S0034-4877(10)80017-5 |bibcode= 2010RpMP...65..231Z }}</ref> exact [[Solitary wave (water waves)|solitary wave]] solutions<ref name={{FengW|2006}}>{{citation|first1= Z. |last1= Feng |first2= X. |last2= Wang|title= Explicit exact solitary wave solutions for the Kundu equation|journal= Phys. Scripta| volume= 64 |year=2006|page= 7|doi= 10.1238/Physica.Regular.064a00007 |s2cid= 122014428 }}</ref> via bilinearization,<ref name={{KakeiEt|1995}}>{{citation|first1= S. |last1= Kakei | others = et al. |title= Bilinearization of a generalised derivative NLS equation|journal= J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.|volume= 64|issue= 5 |year=1995|page= 1519 | doi = 10.1143/jpsj.64.1519|arxiv=solv-int/9501005|bibcode=1995JPSJ...64.1519K|s2cid= 14814702 }}</ref> and Darboux transformation<ref name={{GengT|1999}}>
{{citation|first1= X. |last1= Geng|first2= H. |last2= Tam |title=Darboux transformation and soliton solutions for generalised NLS equation|journal= J. Phys. Soc. Jpn.| volume= 68 |issue= 5|year=1999|page= 1508 |doi=10.1143/jpsj.68.1508 | bibcode = 1999JPSJ...68.1508G}}</ref><ref name={{Lu|2013}}>{{citation|first= X. |last= Lü |title=Soliton behavior for a generalized mixed nonlinear Schrödinger equation with ''N''-fold Darboux transformation|journal=Chaos| volume= 23 |issue= 3 |year=2013|page= 033137 |doi=10.1063/1.4821132|pmid= 24089973 |bibcode=2013Chaos..23c3137L}}</ref> together with the [[orbital stability]] for such solitary wave solutions.<ref name={{ZhangEt|2009}}>{{citation|first1= W. |last1= Zhang | others = et al. |title=Orbital stability of solitary waves for Kundu equations|journal= J. Diff. Equations| volume= 274 |issue= 5 |year=2009 | page= 1591 | doi= 10.1016/j.jde.2009.05.008 |bibcode= 2009JDE...247.1591Z |doi-access= }}</ref>

The Kundu equation has been applied to various physical processes such as [[fluid dynamics]], [[plasma physics]], and [[nonlinear optics]].<ref name={{ZhangEt|2009}}/> It is linked to the mixed nonlinear Schrödinger equation through a [[gauge transformation]] and is reducible to a variety of known integrable equations such as the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]] (NLSE), derivative NLSE, higher nonlinear derivative NLSE, Chen–Lee–Liu, Gerjikov-Vanov, and [[Kundu–Eckhaus equation]]s, for different choices of the parameters.<ref name={{kundu|1984}}/>

==Kundu-Eckhaus equation==

A generalization of the [[nonlinear Schroedinger equation|nonlinear Schrödinger equation]] with additional quintic nonlinearity and a nonlinear dispersive term was proposed in the form<ref name={{kundu|1984}} />
{{NumBlk||<math display="block"> \psi_t+\psi_{xx} -2 c |\psi|^2\psi+\kappa^2|\psi|^4\psi \pm 2i
\kappa (| \psi|^2)_x \psi=0, </math>|{{EquationRef|3}}}}
which may be obtained from the '''Kundu Equation''' {{EquationNote|2|(2)}}, when restricted to <math>\alpha =0</math>. The same equation, limited further to the particular case <math>c =0,</math> was introduced later as [[Eckhaus equation|the Eckhaus equation]], following which equation {{EquationNote|3|(3)}} is presently known as the '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation. The '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation can be reduced to the nonlinear Schrödinger equation through a nonlinear transformation of the field and known therefore to be gauge equivalent integrable systems, since they are equivalent under the [[gauge transformation]].

===Properties and Applications===
The '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation is associated with a [[Lax pair]], higher [[conserved quantity]], exact [[soliton|soliton solution]], [[rogue wave]] solution etc. Over the years various aspects of this equation, its generalizations and link with other equations have been studied. In particular, relationship of '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation with the Johnson's hydrodynamic equation near criticality is established,<ref name={{kundu|1987}} >
{{citation | first=A. |last=Kundu |title= Exact solutions in higher order nonlinear equations gauge transformation| journal= Physica D | volume=25 |issue=1–3 | year=1987|pages=399–406 | doi=10.1016/0167-2789(87)90113-8|bibcode=1987PhyD...25..399K}}
</ref> its [[discretization]]s,<ref name={{levi|2009}} >
{{citation | first1=D. |last1=Levi| first2=C. |last2=Scimiterna |title=The Kundu–Eckhaus equation and its discretizations| journal= J. Phys. A | volume= 42|issue=46| year=2009|article-number=465203 | doi=10.1088/1751-8113/42/46/465203|arxiv=0904.4844| bibcode=2009JPhA...42T5203L|s2cid=15460432}}</ref> reduction via Lie symmetry,<ref name={{tooman|2013}} >
{{citation | first1= M.|last1=Toomanian| first2= N.|last2=Asadi |title= Reductions for Kundu-Eckhaus equation via Lie symmetry analysis
| journal= Math. Sci. | volume=7 | year=2013
|page=50 |doi=10.1186/2251-7456-7-50 |doi-access=free}}
</ref> complex structure via Bernoulli subequation,<ref name={{beok|2015}} >
{{citation | first1=H. M. |last1= Beokonus|
first2=Q. H. |last2= Bulut |title= On the complex structure of Kundu-Eckhaus equation via Bernoulli subequation function method
| journal= [[Waves in Random and Complex Media]] | volume= 25 | year=2015
|doi=10.1080/17455030.2015.1080392|s2cid= 120955017}}
</ref> bright and dark soliton solutions via [[Bäcklund transform]]ation<ref name={{wang|2015}}>
{{citation | first1=H. P. |last1= Wang| others = et al. |title= Bright and Dark solitons and Baecklund transformation for the Kundu–Eckhaus equation
| journal= Appl. Math. Comp. | volume= 251 | year=2015
|pages= 233–242|doi= 10.1016/j.amc.2014.11.014}}
</ref> and Darboux transformation<ref name={{Qui|2015}} >{{citation |
first1= D. |last1= Qui| others = et al.
|title=The Darbaux transformation and the Kundu–Eckhaus equation| journal= Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A |
volume= 451 | year=2015|page= 20150236}}</ref> with the associated [[rogue wave]] solutions,<ref name={{XWang|2014}} >
{{citation | first1= Xin |last1= Wang| others = et al. |title= Higher-order rogue wave solutions of the Kundu–Eckhaus equation
| journal= Phys. Scripta | volume= 89 |issue= 9| year=2014
|article-number= 095210 | doi=10.1088/0031-8949/89/9/095210|bibcode=2014PhyS...89i5210W|s2cid= 54651403}}
</ref><ref name={{Ohta|2012}} >
{{citation | first1= Y. |last1= Ohta| first2= J. |last2= Yang |title= General higher order rogue waves and their dynamics in the NLS equation
| journal= Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A | volume= 468 |issue= 2142| year=2012
|pages= 1716–1740|doi= 10.1098/rspa.2011.0640|arxiv=1110.5873|s2cid= 118617979}}</ref> are studied.

=== RKL equation ===

A multi-component generalisation of the '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation {{EquationNote|3|(3)}}, known as '''Radhakrishnan, Kundu and Laskshmanan''' (RKL) equation was proposed in nonlinear optics for [[fiber optics]] communication through [[soliton]] pulses in a [[birefringent]] non-Kerr medium<ref name={{RKL|1999}} >
{{citation | first1= R. | last1= Radhakrishnan | first2= A. | last2= Kundu
|first3= M. |last3= Lakshmanan|title= Coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations with cubic-quintic nonlinearity: integrability and soliton interaction in non-Kerr media | journal= Phys. Rev. E | volume= 60|issue= 3| year=1999 | pages= 3314–3323 | doi = 10.1103/physreve.60.3314 | pmid= 11970146 | arxiv=solv-int/9905006 | bibcode=1999PhRvE..60.3314R | s2cid= 24223614}}
</ref> and analysed subsequently for its exact soliton solution and other aspects in a series of papers.<ref name={{Biswas|2009}} >
{{citation | first1= A. |last1= Biswas|title= 1-soliton solution of the generalized Radhakrishnan, Kundu, Lakshmanan equation
| journal= Physics Letters A | volume= 373 |issue= 30| year=2009
|pages= 2546–2548 | doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2009.05.010|bibcode=2009PhLA..373.2546B}}
</ref><ref name={{Zhang|2008}}>
{{citation | first1= J. L. |last1= Zhang| first2= M. L. |last2= Wang |title= Various exact solutions for two special type RKL models
| journal= Chaos, Solitons & Fractals | volume= 37 |issue= 1| year=2008
|page= 215 | doi=10.1016/j.chaos.2006.08.042|bibcode=2008CSF....37..215Z}}</ref><ref name="{{ Ganji|2008}}" >
{{citation | first1= D. D. |last1= Ganji| others = et al. |title= Exp-function based solution of nonlinear Radhakrishnan, Kundu and Laskshmanan (RKL) equation
| journal= Acta Appl. Math. | volume= 104 |issue= 2| year=2008
|pages= 201–209 | doi=10.1007/s10440-008-9252-0|s2cid= 121155452}}
</ref><ref name={{Chung|2011}}>
{{citation | first1= X. I. N. |last1= Chun-gang| others = et al. |title= New soliton solution of the generalized RKL equation through optical fiber transmission | journal= J. Anhui Univ. (Natural Sc Edition) | volume= 35 | year=2011 | page= 39}}</ref>

===Quantum Aspects===

Though the '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation (3) is gauge equivalent to the [[nonlinear Schroedinger equation|nonlinear Schrödinger equation]], they differ with respect to their [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]] structures and field commutation relations. The [[Hamiltonian operator]] of the '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' equation quantum field model given by
:<math> {H}
=\int dx \left[ : \left( (\psi^\dagger_x \psi_x + c \rho^2
+i \kappa \rho (\psi^\dagger \psi_x- \psi^\dagger_x \psi) \right):
 +\kappa^2
(\psi^\dagger \rho ^2 \psi) \right], \ \ \ \ \rho \equiv (\psi^\dagger \psi)
</math>

and defined through the [[bosonic field]] operator [[commutation relation]] <math> [\psi (x), \psi^\dagger(y)]= \delta(x-y)</math>, is more complicated than the well-known bosonic Hamiltonian of the quantum nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Here <math>\ : \ \ : \ </math> indicates [[normal ordering]] in bosonic operators. This model corresponds to a double <math>\delta </math>-function interacting Bose gas and is difficult to solve directly.

=== One-dimensional Anion gas ===

However, under a nonlinear transformation of the field below:
:<math>
\tilde \psi (x)= e^{-i \kappa \int^x_{- \infty}
 \psi^\dagger (x') \psi (x') dx'} \psi (x)
</math>

the model can be transformed to:
:<math>
\tilde H=\int dx \vdots \left(
\tilde \psi^\dagger_x \tilde \psi_x
 + c (\tilde \psi^\dagger \tilde \psi)^2 \right) \vdots
, </math>

i.e. in the same form as the quantum model of the [[nonlinear Schroedinger equation|Nonlinear Schrödinger equation]] (NLSE), though it differs from the NLSE in its contents, since now the fields involved are no longer bosonic operators but exhibit [[anyon|anion]] like properties.
:<math>
\tilde \psi^\dagger (x_1) \tilde \psi^\dagger (x_2)=e^{i \kappa\epsilon (x_1-x_2)}
\tilde \psi^\dagger (x_2)\tilde \psi^\dagger (x_1) ,
\ \tilde \psi (x_1) \tilde \psi^\dagger (x_2)=e^{-i \kappa \epsilon (x_1-x_2)}
\tilde \psi^\dagger (x_2)\tilde \psi (x_1)+ \delta (x_1-x_2)
</math>
etc. where

<math>
\epsilon (x-y)= + \ , -, 0 \ \ ~ </math> for <math>\ ~ x >y, \ x< y, \ \ x = y ,</math>

though at the coinciding points the bosonic [[commutation relation]] still holds. In analogy with the Lieb Limiger model of <math> \delta </math> function [[bose gas]], the quantum '''Kundu-Ekchaus''' model in the N-particle sector therefore corresponds to a one-dimensional (1D) anion gas interacting via a <math>\delta</math> function interaction. This model of interacting anion gas was proposed and exactly solved by the [[Bethe ansatz]] in
<ref name={{kundu|1999}} >
{{citation | first=A. |last=Kundu |title= Exact solution of double-delta function Bose gas through interacting anyon gas
| journal= Phys. Rev. Lett. | volume=83|issue=7 | year=1999
|pages=1275–1278 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.83.1275 | bibcode=1999PhRvL..83.1275K|arxiv=hep-th/9811247|s2cid=119329417 }}
</ref>
and this basic anion model is studied further for investigating various aspects of the 1D anion gas as well as extended in different directions.
<ref name={{Batch|2006}} >
{{citation | first1= M.T. |last1=Batchelor | first2= X. W.. |last2=Guan |
first3= N.. |last3=Oelkers |title= One-dimensional interacting anyon gas: low energy properties and Haldane exclusion statistics
| journal= Phys. Rev. Lett. | volume=96|issue=21 | year=2006
|article-number=210402 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.96.210402 | bibcode=2006PhRvL..96u0402B | pmid=16803221|arxiv=cond-mat/0603643 | hdl=10440/969 |s2cid=28378363 |url=http://espace.library.uq.edu.au/view/UQ:80501/UQ80501.pdf}}</ref><ref name={{Girar|2006}} >
